text: A grant unto JosErn Whitwortii, of Manchester, in the county of Lancaster, engineer, for his invention of " Certain improvements in machinery for spinning and doubling cotton, wool, and other fibrous substances "; 6 months.

A grant unto William Hawks the yor, of Gateshead, in the county of Durham, iron manufacturer, for his new invented sundry improvements in constructing and making chains, for the use of mines and other purposes ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within England and Wales and the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within 6 calendar months from the date thereof. By writ, &c.

A grant unto William Westley Richards, of Birmingham, in the county of Warwick, gun maker, for his invented " Improvement in the construction of gun and pistol locks "; to hold, &c ; two months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Eugene, of London, gentl, his execrs, admrs, and assigns, of his new invencon of an engine for raising water, whereby one horse by his present method shall raise as great a quantity of water in the same time and height as twenty horses, and that one man by the same principal of power may be able to raise 60 tunns in an hour by a bucket engine; to hold the same within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years from the date hereof according to the statute in such case made and provided ; and a clause is inserted for obliging him particularly to describe the nature of his said invencon, by an instrument in writing under his hand and seal, to be inrolled in the High Court of Chancery within two kalendar months from the date hereof. Witness His Matie at Westm1" the 13th day of November, in the year above. By writt, &c.

A grant unto Aime Nicolas Derode, of No. 37, Rue St. Roch, Paris, France, gentleman, for his invention of " A certain process for uniting cast iron to cast iron and other metals, and for uniting other metals together "; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto William Newton, of Chancery Lane, in the county of Middlesex, civil engineer, for " Certain improvements in the manufacture of sugar from the cane"; being a communication ; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto Patrick Welden, of the city of Dublin, merchant, of his new invented method of bleaching and whitening linen and yarn by a composition entirely new, whereby they will be bleached and whitened better, cheaper, and in less than half the time at present imployed in bleaching and whitening them ; to hold to him, his exors, adfhors, and assigns, within England, Wales, the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, and all the colonies and plantations abroad, for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute; with a clause to inroll the same within four calendar months from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westm1-, the 2nd day of March, in the year above. By Avrit, &c.

A grant unto Sir Thomas Cochrane, knight, commonly called Lord Cochrane, of Regent Street, in the county of Middlesex, for his invented '* Apparatus to facilitate excavating, sinking, and mining"; to hold, &c ; six mouths. Bv writ. &r.

A grant unto Connor William O'Leary, of Tralee, in the county of Kerry, in Ireland, corn merchant, for his invention of " Certain improvements in the methods of producing power for the discharge of weapons and missiles, and other purposes "; 6 months.

A grant unto John Garnett, of Liverpool, in the county of Lancaster, merchant, and Joseph Williams, of Liverpool, aforesaid, manufacturing chemist, for their invention of " An improved method of manufacturing salt from brine "; 6 months.

A grant unto John Scott, of the county of Edinburgh, in that part of the kingdom of Great Britain called Scotland, surveyor of land, of his new invented art 8c mystery of making glass from one single material ; and also has found out & invented the art & mystery of making pig iron from one certain material never before used; to hold to him, his execis, admls, & assigns, within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within 4 kalendar months from the date hereof. Witness His Matie at Westm1', the 23rd day of January, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A erant unto Ricuarp Garrett, of Leiston Works, near Sax- | | mundham, in the county of Suffolk, agricultural implement maker, for his invention of “ Improvements in machinery for drilling, threshing, and cutting agricultural produce”; 6 months.

A grant unto Isaac Harres, of Rosedale Abbey, in the county of York, farmer, for his invention of “Certain improvements in machines or machinery for rowing, sowing, and manuring land”; 6 months ; colonies.
A grant unto Alexandre Debain, manufacturer, of Paris, in the kingdom of France, for his invention of " Certain improvements applicable to keyed musical instruments "; six months.

A grant unto Chester Gould, of Red Lyon Street, Clerkenwell, in the county of Middlesex, gentleman, for a new invented hydrometer, on a new principle, for the purpose of ascertaining the strength of spirits, and determining the specific gravity of fluids ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month, and also a clause for supplying the commissioners of excise with all such articles of the said invention as he shod be required, upon such reasonable prices and terms as shall be settled for that purpose by the said commrs of excise. W. H. M. at Westminster, the 3d day of September, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto William Johnson, of Droitwich, in the county of Worcester, gentleman, for his invented " Certain improvements in the mode of process and form of apparatus for the manufacturing of salt and other purposes"; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Miers, of the precinct of the Savoy, in the county of Middx, jeweller, for his invented new method of accelerating the evaporation of liquid or fluid bodies, destroying the noxious and offensive effluvia arising from spent soap lyes, or other liquid, fluid, or solid substance, and generating an increased degree of heat without additional fuel ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwickupon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within two calendar months from the date thereof. By writ, &c.
A grant unto JosepH Quick, of Sumner Street, Southwark, in the county of Surrey, engineer, for his invention of “Improvements in steam engines”; 6 months.

A grant unto Louis Gov la Blache, of the parish of Sc George Bloomsbury, in the county of Middx, surgeon, of his new invented medicine, which he calls Royal Military Drops ; to hold to him, his exec1'3, admrs, & assigns, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, and His Matie's colonies and plantacons abroad, for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within 4 kalendar months from the date hereof. Witness His Matie at Westm1, the 12th day of November, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Benjamin Parsons, of York Road, Lambeth, in the county of Surrey, engineer, and Edward Esdaile, of the City Saw Mills, City Road, machine sawyer, for their invention of " An improved machine for cutting leaves of wood, such as those commonly called scale board "; 6 months.

A grant unto Francois Durand, engineer, and Onesiphore Pecqueur, engineer, of Paris, for their invention of " Improvements in forming leather into tubes, cylinders, switches, cases, sheaths, hats, and other articles"; 6 months.

A grant to Thomas Neale of the sole vse and benefitt of his new invencon of well makeing of Steele equivalent to Corinthian Steele, never yet made in England, with materialls of the native growth; to hold to him, the said Thomas Neale, his exors, adffis, and assigns, for the terme of 14 yeares according to the statute in that case made and provided ; with other vsuall clauses. Testily apud Westm, 15t0 7bris, a° pdcto. By writt, &c.

A grant unto John Isaac Hawkins, of Pancras Vale, in the parish of Saint Pancras, in the county of Middlesex, civil engineer, for " Certain improved instruments for facilitating the cure of disease by administering galvanic influence into the human body "; being a communication from a foreigner residing abroad ; to extend to the colonies ; six months. By writ, &r.
A grant unto Malcom Muir, of the city of Glasgow, for his invtd "Certain machinery for preparing boards for flooring and other similar purposes"; to hold, &c ; two months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto William Wood, of Summer Hill, in the county of Northumberland, near Newcastle-upon-Tyne, for his invented " The application of a battering ram to the purpose of working coal in mines "; to hold, &c; four months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Anthony Schick, of Gracechurch Street, in the city of London, merchant, for his invented method or process of roasting coffee ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within two calendar months from the date thereof. By writ, &c.
A grant unto Samuel Burrows, of Sheffield, in the county of York, fork manufacturer, for his invention of " Certain improvements in the manufacture of knives"; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto MABG LARIVIERE, now residing N° 21, Frith Street. Soho, in the coy of Middx, mechanician, late of Geneva, in Switzerland, for his " Perfected machine for perforating metal, plateof gold, silver, tin. platina, brass, or copper, being applicable to all the purposes of sieves hitherto employing either canvas, linen, or wire"; to hold, &c ; two months. By writ, &c.
A grant unto Stephen R. Parkhurst, of Liverpool, in the county of Lancaster, machinist, for his invention of "A method of propelling vessels "; 6 months.

A grant unto Josrpu Hatt, of Cambridge, in the county of Cambridge, grocer and draper, for his invention of “A seed and dust disperser, which is particularly applicable to the freeing of corn and other plants from insects ”; six months.

A speciall lycence graunted unto George Tomlyn, his executo1-3, administrators, and assignes, for the terme of twelve yeares from the day of the date hereof, being the remaynder of 14 yeares formerly graunted by His Matie to the said George Tomlyn, which the said George Tomlyn hath surrendered to His Ma,ie, for the sole printing with a rolling printing presse and engraven plates upon velum & parchm* of the name & tytle of His Matie, his hcires & successo1"3, & also of his royal consort the Queene, with the imperial armes & badges & every of them, with all pfitts & advants thereunto belonging — paying into His Matie's exchequer 12 nobles p annu dureing the said terme. Teste apud Westm'", 28 Martii, 15 Car 2di. By writt of privy seale.

A grant unto James Irwin, confectioner, of the parish of Saint George, Hanover Square, in the county of Middlesex, of his new discovered method, never before used, of making black currant drops and lozenges of fruits, which, being of great efficacy in the cure of sore throats, obstinate coughs, and hoarsenesses, he conceives maybe of great benefit to His Majesty's subjects ; to hold to him, his exors, adniors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within four calendar months from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westm1", the 5th day of March, in the year above. By writ, &c.
Agrantunto George Armstrong, of Neweastle-upon-Tyne, esquire, for his invention of " Certain improvements in steam engines "; 6 months.
A grant unto William Brunton, of Neath, Glamorgan, engineer, for his invention of " An improved method or means of dressing ores and separating metals or minerals from other substances"; 6 months.

A grant unto James How, of Bovingdon, near Hemel Hempstead, in the county of Herts, farmer, for his new invented plough upon an improved construction ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. W. H. M. at Westmr, the 30th day of Octr, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto William Edwards Staite, of Lombard Street, in the city of London, gentleman, for his invention of " Improvements in the construction of galvanic batteries, in the formation of magnets, and in the application of electricity and magnetism for the purpose of lighting and signalizing ; as also a mode or modes of employing the said galvanic batteries, or some of them, for the purpose of obtaining chemical products "; parts of whicli improvements have been communicated to him by a foreigner residing abroad ; colonies.

A grant unto William White, of Garlick Hill, in the city of London, tallow chandler, of his invented machine by which the noxious or foul air may be expelled in a short interval of time from any mines, ship, gaol, hospital, chamber, or other close place, and fresh cool air introduced in its stead, however calm the atmosphere or however warm or sultry the season or climate ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and asss, within Engd, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 yrs pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inrol the same within one calendar month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at West1-, the 12th day of May, in the year above. By writ, &c.
A grant unto Joseph Rock, jun., of Birmingham, in the county of Warwick, factor, for his invention of " Improvements in the construction of locks "; 6 months.
A grant unto Edward Johnson, of Nelson Square, Blackfriars Road, in the county of Surrey, surgeon, for his invention of " Improvements in apparatus for bathing "; 6 months.
A grant unto Tuomas Lambert, of Hampstead Road, in the county of Middlesex, pianoforte manufacturer, for his invention of ‘ Certain improvements in pianofortes”; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto John Lane, of Liverpool, and John Taylor, of Liverpool, engineers, for their invention of " Improvements in engines, boilers, and pumps, in railway carriages, in propelling vessels, in the construction of boats, in extinguishing fire, and in brewing "; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto Richard Summers Harford, of Ebbw Vale Iron Works, in the parish of Aberystwith, in the county of Monmouth, iron master (being one of the people called Quakers), for his invtd "Improvement in the heating processes in the manufacture of bar, rod, sheet, and other description of malleable iron, whether the same may have been previously prepared by the pudling or other modes of refining"; to hold, &c ; four months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Robert Tripp, of the city of Bristol, woollen draper, for his invtd improved hussar garter, with elastic springs and fastenings; and also elastic springs for pantaloons and other articles ; to hold, &c ; 6 mo5.

A grant unto Eugene de Beuret (commonly called Viscount de Beuret), of 28, Moorgate Street, in the city of London, for " Certain improvements in the construction of railroads and tramroads, to facilitate the ascent and descent of hills and inclined plains"; being a communication from a foreigner residing abroad ; 2 months.

A grant unto James Gathercole, of Eltham, in the county of Kent, envelope manufacturer, for his invention of "Improvements in the manufacture and ornamenting of envelopes ; parts of which improvements arc applicable to other descriptions of stationery, and in the machinery, apparatus, or means to be used therein "; 6 months ; colonics.

A grant unto GeOitge Shefi/EY, of Horseley Down, in the borough of Southwark, leather dresser, of his new discovered and introduced millstones, which, placed horizontally and worked with wind or water, will reduce to powder bark for tanning leather, and Brazil wood, logwood, fustick, madder, indigo, saltpetre, and all other woods, drugs, roots, minerals, and colours used in dying, in a quicker, less expensive, and better manner than the present method ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within four calendar months from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westm1, the 27th day of June, in the year above. By writ, &c.

William Jennens, kn1, haveing attained to the knowledge of erecting certain bainds to sweat, wash, & bath in, never yet used in any of His Matie's dominions, which in remote parts have been found of great advantage for pservation of health, by speedy removall of severall diseases incident to the body of man, and that he hath erected the same to be as beneficiall as any other bainds in any part of the world, His Matie, at his spiall instance, is pleased to grant to him & to Charles Systed, of London, merchant, lycence to use it, and all benefitt arriseing thereby ; to hold to them, their exors, admors, & assignes, for 14 years according to the statute ; and with clauses & non obstantes usuall in like grants. T. I£ apud Westm, 25° Mary, anno pdco. By writt, &c.
A grant unto J ohn Winter, of Acton, in the county of Middlesex, esq1*, for his invtd " Certain improvements on chimney caps, and in the application thereof"; to hold, &c ; two months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto George Alexander Miller, of N° 179, Piccadilly, in the parish of Saint James, Westminster, in the county of Middlesex, wax chandler, for his invention of "An improvement in lamps "; two months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Dickinson, of the parish of Saint Martin, Ludgate, in the city of London, stationer, for his invented certain improvements on his patent machinery for cutting and placing paper, and also certain machinery for the manufacture of paper by a new method ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon- Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within six calendar months from the date thereof. By writ, &c.

9431 A grant unto JouN STEPHEN Woorricu, of Birmingham, in the county of Warwick, chemist, for his invention of “ Improvements in coating with metal the surface of articles formed of metal or metallic alloys”; 6 months.
A grant unto Edward Welch, of Liverpool, in the county of Lancaster, architect, for his invention of " Certain improvements in the construction of bricks "; 6 months.

A grant unto Benjamin Cook, of Birmingham, in the county of Warwick, gilt toy maker, for his invented u Improved method of making and constructing rollers or cylinders, both solid and hollow, which will be found useful in various manufactories in this kingdom"; to hold, &c ; sixmo8. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Slater, of Liverpool, in the county palatine of Lancaster, gent., for his invented certain improvements upon sawing mills, or machines for sawing all kinds of timber ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon- Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within four calendar months from the date thereof ; and also with a clause for supplying His Majesty's service with all such articles of the said invention as shall be required by the mas1' gen1 of our ordnance and commrs of our navy for the time being. By writ, &c.

William Pawley and Edw'd Dallow informing His Matie that they, with their long study & labour, have found out a new way or art for dreyning mynes & other necessary uses never heretofore found out or vsed by another, which being putt into practice may be of great advantage to his subjects in general!, upon their humble petition His Matie is pleased to grant them licence, sole poAver, & priviledge to vse, practize, & exercise the said art & invencon in England & Wales, & to have & enioy the sole benefitt & advantage ariseing thereby ; to hold & enioy the sd licence, authority, & other the pmsses from the date hereof for the terme of 14 yeers according to the statute in that case made ; with other clauses & non obstant vsuall in like grant. Teste I£ apud Westm, 25 Junij, anno 33° C. 2di supdict. By writt, &c.

A grant unto John McInnes, of Auchenreoch and of Woodburn, in that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called Scotland, esq., for his invented " The manufacture or preparation of certain substances, which he denominates ' the British tapioca'; and the cakes and flour to be made from the same"; to hold, &c ; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Ainslie, of Alperton, in the county of Middlesex, brick and tile manufacturer, for his invention of <; Certain improvements in the arrangements for the manufacture of bricks, tiles, and other similar articles from clay and other plastic substances, and in the machinery or apparatus for the manufacture of bricks "; 6 months. 4 0 2

A grant unto Charles Downing, of Bideford, in the coy of Devon, gent., for his invented or found out " Certain improvements in fowling pieces and other fire arms"; to hold, &c ; two months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Bentinck, esquire, Captain in His Majesty's Royal Navy, and William Cole, of the parish of Saint Mary, Lambeth, in the county of Surry, engine maker, of their chain pump, entirely upon a new construction, for raising water out of ships, or draining of lands, or for any other purpose where a chain pump can be applied or made of use ; to hold to them, their executors, admors, & assigns, within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within 4 calendar months from the date hereof. W. H. M. at W., the 1 7th day of Janry, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Syeds, of Mill Street, in the parish of Saint Mary Magdalen, Bermondsey, in the borough of Southwark, and county of Surry, mariner, of his new invented machine or instrument called an improved quadrant, for determining the altitude at sea when no horizon can be found, and for the easier ascertaining the longitude ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, & ass3, within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon- Tweed, for the term of 14 yrs pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inrol the same within one calendar month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westr, the 21st day of Janry, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Collinge, of Buxton Place, in the parish of Saint Mary, Lambeth, in the count}^ of Surry, patent axle tree maker, of his new invented improvement upon sugar mills, which will occasion less power to work them, and are not liable to be out of order ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, & asss, within Engd, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, and also within His Majesty's colonies & plantations abroad, for the term of 14 yrs pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at West1", the 30th day of October, the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Thomas Motley, of the city of Bristol, ironmonger, for his invented improved method of manufacturing letters or characters for signs, shew boards, fronts of shops, houses, and other places, and for any other purpose of composing and indicating names or words in relief in a conspicuous manner ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that s s part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute; with a clause to inroll the same within two calendar months from the date thereof. By writ, &c.

Middx, smith, for his invented machine or instrument; to be applied to stoves or grates, for preventing accidents by fire, and whereby the fires in stoves or grates may l)e" put out and extinguished with safety and facility ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. J3y writ, &c.

A grant unto Elijah Galloway, of the London Road, in the parish of Saint George the Martyr, in the county of Surrey, engineer, for his invented "Improved rotary steam engine"; to hold, &c ; six months. By writ, &c. , of Ipswich, in the coy of Suffolk,
A grant unto James Jounston, of Willow Park, Greenock, esq’, for his inyention of “ Improvements in obtaining motive power ”; six months. 4C 2

A grant unto William Brown, of the city of Glasgow, merchant, for his invention of " Improvements in the manufacture of porcelain, china, pottery, and earthenware ; and which improvements are also in part applicable to the manufacture of paper and to the preparation of certain pigments or painters colours"; 6 months.
A grant unto George Brown, of Caperthorne, near Congleton, in the county of Chester, land agent, for his invention of " A new seed and manure drill plough"; 6 months.

A grant unto Peter Armand Le Comte de Fontainemoreau, of Skinners Place, Sise Lane, London, for " A new and improved mode or method of paving and covering roads and other ways or surfaces"; being a communication ; 6 months.

A grant unto Robert William Sievier, of Upper Holloway, in the county of Middlesex, gentleman, for his invention of " Improvements in weaving and printing or staining textile goods or fabrics"; 6 months; colonies.
A grant unto John Fuller, of Beacham Well, in the county of Norfolk, farmer, for his invention of "Improvements in apparatus for sowing corn or other seed ": 6 months.
A grant unto Nathaniel Benjamin, of Camber well, in the county of Surrey, gentleman, for " Improvements in the manufacture of type "; being a communication ; six months.

A grant unto John To will Rutt, of Basinghall Street, London, John Tretton, of Sl Andrews Hill, London, and John Webb, of Clapton, in the county of Middx, for their invented various improvements in the construction of machines for making cards for carding wool, cotton, flax, silk, and all substances capable of being carded ; to hold to them, their exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwickupon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within two calendar months from the date thereof. By writ, &c.

A grant unto William Lester, of Cotton End, in the parish of Hardingstone, in the county of Northampton, patent harrow and chaff engine manufacturer, for his further new improvements upon an engine or machine for cutting hay and straw into chaff, for which he obtained former Letters Patent ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. W. H. M. at Westmr, the 17th day of Feby, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Joshua Wheeler, mercer, of the city of Worcester, of his new invented method to prepare woollen cloth & hatts so as to keep out more than a day's or week's rain, without impairing either the beauty or strength of the cloth or hatts ; to hold to him, his execrs, admrs, or assignes j within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, for the term of 1 4 years pursuant to the statute in that behalf, with a clause to inroll within 4 calendar months from the date hereof. Witnesses, Thomas Archbishop of Canterbury, &c, at Westmr, the 27th day of June, in the year above. By writt, &c.

A grant unto George Fergusson Wilson, managing director of Price's Patent Candle Company, Vauxhall, David Wilson, of Wandsworth, esquire, James Ctiilds, of Putney, esquire, and John Jackson, gentleman, of Vauxhall aforesaid, all in the county of Surrey, for their invention of " Improvements in presses and matting ; and in the process of and apparatus for treating fatty and oily matters ; and in the manufacture of candles and night lights"; 6 months ; colonies.
A grant unto William 1 Iannis Taylor, of Lambeth, in the county of Surrey, csq,v, for his invention of " Certain improvements in propelling machinery"; six months.

A grant unto Eardley Norton, of Sl John Street, in the parish of Sl Sepulchre, in the county of Middlesex, clock and watch maker, of his new invented clock, which strikes the hours and parts upon a principle intirely new, and a watch which repeats the hours and parts, so concisely contrived as to admit of being conveniently contained, not only in a watch, but also its appendage, such as a key, seal, or tricket ; to hold to him, his exors, adrhors, and asss, within England, Wales, the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, and all the colonies and plantations abroad, for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with aclause to inroll the same within four calendar months from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westmr, the second day of May, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Henry Mapple, of Child's Hill, Hendon, in the county of Middlesex, machinist, for his invention of " Improvements in apparatus for transmitting electricity between distant places, and in electric telegraphs"; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto Christopher Irwin, of the parish of S11 Martin-in-the- Fields, in the county of Middx, esqre, of his new invented method of making a marine observatory and new adapted telescope & almanack for the more exact ascertaining the longitude at sea ; to hold to him, his execrs, admrs, & assigns, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, & His Matie's colonies & plantacons abroad, for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll within 4 kalendar months from the date hereof. Witness His Matie at Westmr, the 2nd day of Dec, in the year above. By writt, &c.

A grant unto John Baptiste Denize, formerly of the city of Paris, but now residing in George Street, Portman Square, in the county of Middlesex, chymisr, for his new invented cement for various purposes ; to hold to him, his exors, adniors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. W. H. M. at Westm1", the 16th day of July, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto William Nicholson, of Soho Square, in the county of Middlesex, gent", for his new invented machinery for the better and more expeditious manufacturing of files ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. W. H. M. at Westmr, the 14th day of August, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A speciall priviledge graunted to John Cason, esq1'., Shewing that whereas hee by his great charge and industrie hath attained to the skill and pfeccon of a more apte and bencficiall meanes for the framing, contrivinge, and makinge of locks, sluces, bridgs, cutts, cranes, mills, dames, and other invencons necessarie and convenient for grindinge of corne, raisinge of water, makinge of rivers and streames navigable and passable for boats, keeles, and other vessells, not yet used or practised by anie other within His MatiLS realmes and dominions, His Matie doth hereby graunte unto the said John Cason, his executors, administrators, deputies, and assignes, free licence and priviledge within the realme of England, dominion of Wales, and town of Bar wick, in places meete and convenient, duringe the terme of xxjtie yeares next ensuinge, as well to devise, make, direct, pfect, and practise the pmisses and other invencons not repugnant to the laws & statuts of this realme, as also to make & invent all manner of engines and tooles for the pfectinge and pforminge thereof. And for that the effecting & pfectinge of the pmisses will amount to a very great charge, His Matie doth hereby comande & prohibite that no pson or psons whatsoever (other than such as shal be licenced or appointed by the said John Cason, or A. which shall give contentment to him his deputies or assignes, attempt, practise, or go about by anie waie or meanes, directlie or indirectlie, to passe, saile, or remaine upon, in, or by anie the rivers, water sluces, cutts, or dames, so to be cutt, made navigable, or pfected by the said John Cason or his deputies as aforesaid, or intermeddle, practise, use, make, build, or putt in use in or upon the same anie mills, sluces, locks, bridges, or engines, such or the like as by the sd John Cason his deputies or assignes have bin first invented, pfected, or sett up, uppon paine of forfeiture and His Maties high displeasure ; provided that the said John Cason shall not by cullor hereof make, attempt, or cause to be made anie cutt, river, watercourse, or anie other the premisses in or upon anie lands or grounds, place or places, whatsoever, but first compounding & agreeing with the owners thereof. And for avoydinge of maine inconveniences wch maie befall by the obstinacie of some well disposed psons, His Matie doth therefore ordaine that noe pson or psons, owner or owners of anie lands, woods, or wasts, where the said patentee or his assigns shall have necessarie occasion to compound for or in respect of the pmisses, pesume to refuse a reasonable composicon, nor contradict or resist the said John Cason his deputies or servants in pforminge anie of the pmisses offeringe & givinge reasonable composicon as aforesaid, upon paine to His Maties high displeasure to be incurred for their contempt of his Royall will in that behalf — yielding & payinge into His Mal's exchequer yearely, during the said terme, the some of fortie shillings.
